lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Confirm the contact details are real rather than placeholders.
Use a clean LinkedIn URL and align the profile with the résumé.
items.because: Its titles, dates, and accomplishments should match.

items.says: Consider adding your current city.
items.because: Location may matter for the roles you are applying for.

items.says: Make the contact items clickable in the PDF.
Standardize date formatting and use en dashes consistently.
Consider moving the caddie role to Additional Experience.
items.because: Leading with a non-finance role may distract from your financial experience.

items.says: Indicate if the caddie role is temporary or part-time.
items.because: Otherwise recruiters may assume you left finance permanently.

items.says: Replace “about 5 rounds” with an accurate figure or range.
Use present tense if caddying is ongoing.
Emphasize service, judgment, member interaction, or operational responsibility instead of just physical duties.
items.because: The current content does little to support a finance candidacy.

items.says: Specify the tournament’s scale, your responsibilities, and its operational result.
Replace the vague verb “helped.”
items.because: It makes your contribution impossible to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the tournament was a completed event or tournaments are recurring.
items.because: The appropriate tense depends on that distinction.

items.says: Define what “efficiency” measures.
items.because: The 40% metric is too vague to verify.

items.says: Give the baseline and resulting level if available.
Clarify the scope of the automation.
items.because: The entities, accounts, business units, or reconciliations affected are not stated.

items.says: Add the total capital value if it is not confidential.
Clarify whether you built the model, evaluated requests, standardized assumptions, or supported approvals.
State the decision or business impact.
items.because: The bullet stops before showing the consequence of standardization.

items.says: Define what “more than 5% off budget” means.
items.because: It could mean percentage points, a relative percentage, or another measure.

items.says: Add a dollar-materiality threshold if one existed.
items.because: Percentage-only thresholds can overemphasize small accounts.

items.says: Say whether the analysis led to actions, forecast revisions, or decisions.
Clarify the scope implied by “each line.”
items.because: It sounds implausibly broad unless that was literally the process.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is a valuation-methodology error.
items.because: FCFE requires the cost of equity; WACC applies to FCFF or unlevered free cash flow.

items.says: Verify which cash-flow definition and discount rate were actually used.
Add transaction size, valuation range, or the decision supported if permitted.
Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group margin.
items.because: Group margin requires consolidated EBITDA divided by consolidated revenue, or revenue-weighted unit margins.

items.says: Confirm the 45% figure after recalculation.
Explain how forecast error was calculated and over what period.
Identify whether the error measures total cash flow, ending cash, or something else.
Verify that the forecast directly supported the early debt repayment.
items.because: The bullet claims causation.

items.says: Add the interest savings or liquidity benefit if possible.
Consider moving this bullet nearer the top of the Stonebridge section.
items.because: It shows scale and financial impact.

items.says: State how many of the 60 loans were approved and originated.
items.because: “Approved loans” introduces an unstated denominator.

items.says: Confirm that every loan had a full two-year performance window.
items.because: Loans approved late in your tenure may not have had two years of seasoning unless tracked afterward.

items.says: Define default using the bank’s standard.
Avoid implying zero defaults resulted solely from your work.
items.because: Committees, servicing, and economic conditions also affect portfolio performance.

items.says: Add the number of declined applications reviewed.
Explain the analytical method behind the threshold changes.
items.because: It should be clear they were evidence-based rather than simply looser underwriting.

items.says: Define “early defaults” and the observation period.
Be careful attributing the approval-rate change to your findings.
items.because: Approval rates may have changed for other reasons.

items.says: Confirm the comparison used similar applicant populations and economic periods.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for this role.
items.because: The role ended in 2022.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, revised, or maintained the checklist.
Add the number of loans, borrowers, or covenants covered if known.
Explain how and over what period the reduction was measured.
Describe the template’s adoption scope.
items.because: The number of analysts or memos affected, or whether it became standard, is unstated.

items.says: Mention a documented quality-control benefit if there was one.
Confirm the time reduction was representative.
items.because: It should not rest on a single memo.

items.says: Add a valuation date.
items.because: Market price changes over time.

items.says: Explain what is still being updated or give the project an end date.
items.because: The heading dates it as ongoing.

items.says: Consider naming the utility if its identity need not be confidential.
Add major valuation assumptions.
items.because: Terminal value, capital structure, or regulatory drivers would demonstrate analytical depth.

items.says: Treat the 6% proximity to market price cautiously.
items.because: It does not establish that the valuation is correct and may suggest anchoring.

items.says: Clarify whether market price was known before assumptions were finalized.
Focus on the independent investment conclusion, not just closeness to market.
Replace “1-point” with a technically precise unit.
State the direction of the discount-rate change.
Give the base discount rate.
items.because: The sensitivity needs context.

items.says: Check the USD 52 and USD 44 values and whether other assumptions were held constant.
items.because: They must correspond to the stated change.

items.says: Consider showing a broader sensitivity table.
items.because: A single scenario may demonstrate less of the model.

items.says: Specify when the investment club used the work.
items.because: The project is dated as ongoing.

items.says: Clarify whether the club adopted the recommendation, presented it, or merely referenced the materials.
Add the pitch audience size or result if possible.
Add the fund’s approximate assets under management if known.
Clarify your formal role and what “Team of 6” refers to.
items.because: It could mean the analyst team or the whole fund.

items.says: Keep the 2018–2019 project only if it remains relevant and space permits.
items.because: It is less valuable than your professional experience and current valuation project.

items.says: The reference to an FP&A team does not fit a student investment fund.
items.because: A student fund would not ordinarily be described as having one.

items.says: Specify the actual group supported and investment-related work performed.
items.because: The wording is generic and unsupported.

items.says: Identify the benchmark and reporting period if useful.
Add fund size, number of holdings, or reporting frequency.
Clarify what changed besides displaying benchmark returns.
The cash-forecast accomplishment duplicates the Stonebridge bullet.
items.because: The nearly exact duplicate can look like accidental copying or fabrication.

items.says: The USD 600M business and debt repayment do not fit the student fund project.
items.because: They are inconsistent with its dates and context.

items.says: List only tools you can use confidently in an interview or test.
Add genuinely advanced Excel capabilities if they are not already obvious.
Clarify the depth of Bloomberg use.
items.because: Merely accessing a Terminal is not necessarily a marketable skill.

items.says: Standardize capitalization.
items.because: It should match the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Correct the valuation bullets before listing methods they appear to contradict.
items.because: Technical errors elsewhere undermine the methods listed.

items.says: Add more specific methods only where experience supports them.
Remove any method you could not explain and execute in an interview.
Keep the résumé to one page if possible.
Prevent awkward bullet wraps, especially a single word on a new line.
Use either USD or dollar-sign notation consistently.
Consider putting relevant professional experience first, the current valuation project next, and non-finance experience later.
items.because: That order better serves finance applications.

items.says: Put the strongest bullets first within each role.
